# Webspaces

> Webspaces turns a plain HTML file into a walkable, multiplayer 3D world. One `<script>` tag upgrades the page;
> the `<body>` holds the world's objects; CSS transforms place them in space; editing the world in the browser
> edits the HTML and writes it back to where the file lives. Worlds are static files: host them anywhere.

This file is written for both people and AI coding agents. If you are an agent asked to "make a webspace"
or "build a 3D world as a web page", everything you need is here. Produce a single `.html` file.

- Home (itself a webspace): https://webspaces.space
- Engine source (MPL-2.0): https://github.com/webspace-sdk/webspace-engine
- Launch post: https://gfodor.medium.com/rebooting-the-web-in-3d-with-webspaces-9e58847e042c
- Showcase (worlds to read and remix): https://webspaces.space/showcase/
- Starter template (Use this template → enable Pages → live world): https://github.com/webspace-sdk/start
- Recipes (short copy-pasteable pieces: splats, skies, night, shared clicks, animation, SVOX, VR): https://webspaces.space/learn/

## Which engine script to use

- Stable: `<script src="https://webspace.run"></script>`
- Preview, with everything marked **(preview)** below (Gaussian splats, scripting, night skies):
  `<script src="https://webspaces.space/run/0.10.0-alpha.11/webspace.js"></script>`
  Versioned preview URLs never change, so a world that pins one keeps working.

## The smallest world

```html
<html>
  <head>
    <script src="https://webspace.run"></script>
  </head>
  <body></body>
</html>
```

Open it in Chrome (from disk or any HTTPS host) and you spawn in as an avatar. Anyone who opens the same URL
is in the world with you: avatars, voice, and live co-editing, peer to peer.

When hosted over HTTP(S), also place `webspace.service.1.0.1.js` next to the HTML (copy it from
https://webspaces.space/webspace.service.1.0.1.js). It is a tiny service worker that enables cross-origin
isolation, which the engine needs. (Worlds saved by the engine write this file for you.)

## Objects are elements

Every direct child of `<body>` is one object in the world. Its tag chooses what it is:

| Markup | Object |
|---|---|
| `<img src="photo.jpg">` | A picture (GIF/WebP animate) |
| `<video src="clip.mp4" autoplay loop muted>` | A screen. YouTube URLs work. HLS (`.m3u8`) and DASH (`.mpd`) streams work |
| `<audio src="song.mp3">` | A positional sound source |
| `<embed src="paper.pdf#page=3">` | A PDF you can page through |
| `<model src="chair.svox">` | A Smooth Voxel model (plain-text voxel format, see below) |
| `<model src="robot.glb">` | A glTF model (Draco compressed OK) |
| `<model src="garden.spz">` | A Gaussian splat capture (`.spz`, `.ply`, `.splat`) of a real place or thing **(preview)** |
| `<label><h1>Hello</h1></label>` | A text sign, sized to its content |
| `<div>…rich HTML…</div>` | A text page (headings, lists, links, bold, etc.) |
| `<marquee>Welcome</marquee>` | Big outlined banner text |
| `<div style="font-family: emoji">🌵</div>` | A 3D voxel emoji |
| `<a href="other-world.html">` | A link to another world or page. Clicking it in-world follows it like any web link: in place, or in a new tab with `target="_blank"` |

Attributes:
- `id="lamp"`: optional. **(preview)** Any id that starts with a letter and uses letters, digits, `-` or `_`
  is kept, so scripts can find objects with `getElementById`. (The stable engine only keeps 7-character
  lowercase ids like `abc1234` and renames others.) Keep ids stable once a world is published.
- `draggable`: people can grab and move it in-world. Omit to lock it in place.
- `contenteditable`: text people can edit in-world.
- `hidden`: not shown.

Style properties that matter: `transform` (placement, below), and for text: `color`,
`background-color`, `font-family` (`sans-serif`, `serif`, `monospaced`, `fantasy`, `ui-rounded`,
`cursive`, `emoji`), `width: min-content; height: min-content` (shrink-to-fit), `-webkit-text-stroke-color`
(banner outline).

## Placing things: CSS transforms, in centimeters

```html
<img src="sunset.jpg" style="transform: translate3d(0cm, 150cm, -400cm) rotate3d(0, 1, 0, 0.5rad) scale3d(2, 2, 2)">
```

- `translate3d(x, y, z)`: y is up; the default spawn looks toward -z. 100cm = 1 meter. On `flat` terrain the ground is at y = 75cm.
- `rotate3d(ax, ay, az, angle)`: axis + angle (`rad` or `deg`).
- `scale3d(sx, sy, sz)`.
- **(preview)** Any CSS transform list works too: `translate3d(0cm, 300cm, -500cm) rotateX(-0.7rad) rotateY(1.2rad)`,
  `matrix3d(...)`, etc. Use `cm` for lengths.
- An eye-level object 4 meters in front of spawn on `flat` terrain: `translate3d(0cm, 235cm, -400cm)` (ground 75cm + eyes 160cm).
- On `hills`, `plains`, and `islands`, the ground height varies (often 75–200cm near spawn). Use `flat` for predictable
  heights, or add ~150 cm.
- Always give objects a transform. An object without one appears in front of each visitor separately.

## The world itself: `<meta>` tags in `<head>`

```html
<title>My World</title>
<meta name="webspace.environment.type" content="terrain" />
<meta name="webspace.environment.terrain.type" content="islands" />   <!-- islands | hills | plains | flat -->
<meta name="webspace.environment.terrain.seed" content="42" />
<meta name="webspace.environment.terrain.colors.sky" content="#8ec5ff" />
<meta name="webspace.environment.terrain.colors.ground" content="#3b6d3b" />
<!-- other colors: edge, leaves, bark, rock, grass, water -->
<meta name="webspace.environment.spawn_point.transform" content="translate3d(0cm, 0cm, 0cm) rotate3d(0, 1, 0, 0rad)" />
```

**(preview)** Big scenes and night:

```html
<meta name="webspace.environment.fog" content="off" />   <!-- see ~2km instead of the cozy ~25m default -->
<meta name="webspace.environment.wrap" content="off" />  <!-- a plane, not a wrapping torus; needed for far-away objects -->
<meta name="webspace.environment.terrain.colors.sky" content="#05060f" />  <!-- a dark sky color makes night -->
```

**(preview)** A real sky: any equirectangular (360°) image replaces the procedural sky.

```html
<meta name="webspace.environment.sky" content="sky.jpg" />
```

Phone panoramas, 360 cameras, and generated skyboxes all work. Poly Haven (https://polyhaven.com/hdris) has
hundreds of CC0 skies: download the tonemapped JPG, resize it to 4096×2048, and prefer the "puresky" variants,
whose horizon sits cleanly on your terrain. Turn `fog` off to see the whole sky.

Choose a palette on purpose; the world's colors carry most of its mood. Terrain seeds change the land shape.
`<meta name="webspace.projection.type" content="flat" />` makes the file a 2D page instead of a 3D world.
Worlds and pages link to each other with plain `<a>` tags. A folder of them is a *webspace*: a website that has
worlds as well as pages. An `index.html` with a `<nav><ul><li><a href="…">` list defines the site's menu.

## Smooth Voxels (SVOX): 3D models as text

SVOX is "markdown for 3D models". It's plain text, so you can write it by hand or generate it.

```
size = 7
scale = 0.15 0.17 0.15
origin = -y
material lighting = smooth, roughness = 0.25, fade = true, deform = 3
  colors = A:#C11 B:#F60 D:#000 C:#F93
material lighting = smooth, roughness = 1, fade = true, deform = 3
  colors = E:#840 F:#000
voxels
------- --AAA-- --AAA-- --AAA-- ------- ------- -------
--AAA-- -BAAAA- -BAAAA- -BAAAA- -BAAAA- ------- -------
-BADAA- BAAAAAA BAAAAAA BAAAAAA -B---A- ------- -------
-BDDDA- BAAAAAA CAAAAAA CABAAAA -B-E-A- ---E--- ---FF--
-BBDBA- BAAAAAA CAAAAAA CABBAAA -C---A- ------- -------
--BBB-- -BAAAB- -CAAAB- -CAAAB- -CCBBB- ------- -------
------- --BBB-- --CCB-- --CCB-- ------- ------- -------
```

That's an apple. Layout of `voxels`: each **line** is one z slice; within a line, each space-separated
**group** is one y layer, bottom to top; each **character** is one x voxel. `-` is empty; letters are
colors declared in a `material`. `size = x y z` (or one number for a cube). `scale` is meters per voxel.
`origin = -y` puts the model's bottom at its placement point. `deform` smooths the shape and `lighting = smooth` shades it.
The world's cel-shaded look comes from these; keep models small (< 32³) and let smoothing do the work.
Save it as `apple.svox` and add `<model src="apple.svox">`, or paste the text directly into a world.
Full reference: https://svox.glitch.me

## Gaussian splats: real places and things

```html
<model src="scans/my-kitchen.spz" style="transform: translate3d(0cm, 0cm, 0cm) rotate3d(1, 0, 0, 3.14159rad)"></model>
```

**(preview)** Captures from phone apps (Scaniverse, Polycam, Luma, etc.) and 3DGS training exports work. `.spz` is the
recommended format: roughly 10x smaller than `.ply`. Splats keep their real-world scale. Many captures come in
upside down (y-down); flip them with `rotate3d(1, 0, 0, 3.14159rad)` as shown. Pair a splat with a
`flat` terrain world so people can walk around inside it, and turn `fog` off for large places.

Splats respond to CSS compositing: `style="mix-blend-mode: plus-lighter"` makes them additive, so they glow
(great for stars, fire, magic, nebulae), and `opacity` fades them. Splats don't have to be scans: you can
generate them with code. See https://github.com/webspace-sdk/showcase/tree/main/stargazer/make for a
~100-line `.spz` writer and a procedural galaxy.

## Making worlds come alive: it's just the DOM (preview)

A world can include ordinary `<script>` tags. Scripts change the world by changing the document, and hear
about the world through ordinary DOM events. Every visitor runs the same script, so script-driven motion is
naturally in sync for everyone.

```html
<script type="module">
  await webspace.ready;                               // objects exist now

  const gift = document.getElementById("gift001");

  // Animate: set style.transform like any web animation
  (function spin(t) {
    gift.style.transform = `translate3d(0cm, 150cm, -300cm) rotate3d(0, 1, 0, ${t / 1000}rad)`;
    requestAnimationFrame(spin);
  })(0);

  // Interact: in-world clicks and hovers are DOM events
  gift.addEventListener("click", () => webspace.state.set("opened", true));
  gift.addEventListener("pointerenter", () => { /* hovered */ });

  // Shared multiplayer state: everyone in the world sees the same values
  webspace.state.addEventListener("change", e => {
    if (e.detail.key === "opened") gift.hidden = true;
  });

  // Spawn things by adding elements
  document.body.insertAdjacentHTML("beforeend",
    `<div style="font-family: emoji; transform: translate3d(100cm, 150cm, -300cm)">🎉</div>`);

  // Where is the viewer?  webspace.player.position -> { x, y, z } in meters
</script>
```

- Changes made by scripts are *runtime* state. They're never saved into the file, so an animated world
  doesn't rewrite itself. Changes people make in-world (dragging, typing, spawning) are *authored* state and are saved.
- `webspace.state` is a shared key/value store (JSON values, last writer wins), synced peer to peer, and
  late joiners receive it.
- Useful properties: `style.transform`, `style.opacity` and `style.mixBlendMode` (splats), `hidden`,
  `src`/`href` (swaps media), and `innerHTML`/`textContent` of text objects (`sign.innerHTML = "<h1>Score: 5</h1>"`) and emoji objects
  (`bud.textContent = "🌷"`).
- Emoji objects use a built-in voxel emoji set; very new emoji (e.g. 🪨) may not be available.
- Time-based motion (`Date.now()`) looks identical for everyone; use `webspace.state` for things people cause.
- Events: `click`, `pointerenter`, `pointerleave` on body elements. Clicks come from mouse, touch taps, VR controllers and hand pinches alike.

## Virtual reality (preview)

Worlds work in headset browsers (Meta Quest, and other WebXR browsers). An **Enter VR** button appears when a
headset is available; scripts can call `webspace.xr.enterVR()` from a click handler. In VR: thumbstick to move,
snap turn with the right stick, point and pull the trigger to click. Trigger clicks arrive as the same DOM
`click` events, so one script serves desktop and VR. `webspace.xr.isPresenting` tells you which mode you're in.

## Controls (for your README)

WASD to move, drag or Shift to look, Space to jump, `/` to create objects, Ctrl+V to paste images/URLs/SVOX,
drag and drop files in, `~` or `@` to toggle the UI, `?` to hide tips. Hover an object and use the tips shown
to move (right-drag), scale, rotate, or edit voxels.

## Saving and publishing

- **Local**: open the `.html` from disk in Chrome and grant folder access when asked. Edits save back to the
  file (File System Access API).
- **GitHub**: host on GitHub Pages; the world can commit its own edits back to the repo with a fine-grained
  token, so anyone you trust can edit it live.
- **Anywhere static**: it's just HTML plus assets (`.svox`, `.glb`, `.spz`, images) in the same folder.
  Relative `src` paths keep a world portable. Keep `webspace.service.1.0.1.js` beside each world's HTML.

## Taste

Webspaces worlds should feel like places, not tech demos. A strong palette, a sense of arrival at spawn,
a few meaningful objects placed with care, text that speaks to the visitor, and something to do together.
The house style is soft, cel-shaded, and timeless: smooth voxels, flat color, clean type.
